actions: Continue and expand geo-fenced digital campaigns promoting Order Ahead, including a $1 credit for first-time users, across all 12 participating shops. Simultaneously, enhance the loyalty promotion for repeat Order Ahead users with a tiered reward structure for reaching specific visit milestones within March.

Implement a dynamic staffing model in the 12 pilot shops, allowing for real-time adjustments to peak-hour staffing (e.g., adding an extra 'broista' or extending shifts) when Order Ahead volume or drive-through queue times exceed predefined thresholds, ensuring service consistency.
expected_responses: Starbucks will likely continue to fine-tune its mobile order capacity release strategy and A/B testing in its pilot cafés, attempting to mitigate its own service issues. They are unlikely to directly counter our specific promotions but will observe overall market share shifts.

Dunkin will probably continue its focus on value-oriented breakfast meal deals and app-based discounts. They may intensify their own mobile app promotions, but their primary competitive angle remains different from our drive-through beverage focus.

Morning customers, particularly commuters and habitual app users seeking reliable and convenient options, will continue to shift towards Dutch Bros if we maintain our service quality and attractive Order Ahead offers. Café visitors will likely continue to favor Starbucks for in-person experiences, while some customers may still opt for home preparation if perceived inconvenience persists across all options.
answer.rationale: Starbucks' ongoing mobile order capacity issues continue to create frustrated demand among commuters and habitual app users. Our previous actions in January and February successfully attracted these customers. By continuing and slightly expanding our geo-fenced Order Ahead campaigns and loyalty program, we aim to capture a larger share of this switching demand and convert them into loyal, repeat customers. The enhanced loyalty program will further incentivize durable growth, aligning with our goal of making existing-shop growth sustainable. Crucially, the dynamic staffing adjustment is vital to protect our core service proposition – speed and convenience at the drive-through. This proactive measure ensures that increased Order Ahead volume does not overwhelm our lanes or compromise pickup times, preventing customer frustration and reinforcing our commitment to consistent, high-quality service, which is central to our brand identity.
resource_commitments: Allocate $15,000 for geo-fenced digital advertising for Order Ahead promotions and $10,000 for loyalty credits and tiered rewards for repeat Order Ahead users across the 12 shops for March 2027.
Allocate $5,000 for incremental labor costs associated with dynamic, real-time peak-hour staffing adjustments across the 12 shops for March 2027. This is in addition to existing staffing budgets.
